description: Reasoning vault aligned with OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §3.5: horizontal and vertical shifts, reflections, stretches and compressions, even/odd symmetry, and combinations of transformations.

archetypes.name: Apply Function Transformations
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §3.5 — Transformation of Functions
archetypes.coreConcept: Changes outside f affect output values; changes to the input affect the graph horizontally, with the inside sign interpreted in the opposite direction for shifts.
archetypes.mentalModel: Treat the graph as points moving: a horizontal shift changes x-coordinates, a vertical shift changes y-coordinates, and scale/reflection factors act around the relevant axis.

cognitiveTraps.description: Reading f(x-h) as a shift left by h instead of right by h.
Applying an outside scale to input coordinates or an inside scale to output values.
cognitiveTraps.trapFormula: a f(bx) \text{ scales x by }a \text{ and y by }b

archetypes.name: Distinguish Reflections and Symmetry
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §3.5 — Reflections and Even/Odd Functions
archetypes.coreConcept: Replacing x by -x reflects a graph across the y-axis; multiplying function values by -1 reflects it across the x-axis. Even and odd symmetry describe invariance under these transformations.
archetypes.mentalModel: Track which coordinate changes sign: y changes for an x-axis reflection; x changes for a y-axis reflection.
archetypes.governingRelation: f(-x) \text{ reflects across y-axis};\quad -f(x) \text{ reflects across x-axis}

cognitiveTraps.description: Swapping which coordinate changes sign for a reflection across an axis.
Calling a graph odd because it is symmetric about the y-axis rather than the origin.

archetypes.name: Combine Transformations in a Function Rule
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §3.5 — Combining Transformations
archetypes.coreConcept: A transformed rule can combine input scaling, horizontal translation, output scaling/reflection, and vertical translation; the order and location of each operation matter.
archetypes.mentalModel: Read the inside changes first to locate and scale the x-coordinate, then apply outside changes to the y-coordinate.

cognitiveTraps.description: Scaling the vertical shift together with the function when the shift is outside the multiplier.
Interpreting the sign inside the input as the graph's shift direction.
Keeping the algebraic inverse branch that violates a stated transformed-input restriction.
cognitiveTraps.trapFormula: (x-h)^2=c^2 \mapsto x=h-c \text{ without checking the requested side}

cognitiveTraps.description: Expanding (x-h)^2 as x^2-h^2 and omitting the cross term.
